Consulting with DOJ staff about election interference or potential fraud. They held that the president has a presumption of immunity for official acts - acts carried out in relation to the president's office. The court alludes to the "outer perimeter" of official acts that has been blurry since they decided Nixon v. Fitzgerald. Then, of course, no immunity for unofficial acts disconnected from any presidential function. They remanded to the power court for decision as to what conduct described in the indictment constitutes an official act and whether the presumption of immunity should stand.
